body:
The instance uniforms are shared by all materials on that instance. If you don't use explicit indexing, then it is expected for them to overlap. 

Godot doesn't do any special bookkeeping to ensure that parameters don't conflict with each other. It just starts indexing at 0 at the beginning of each shader. 

See the notes in the documentation https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#per-instance-uniforms

This is a common point of confusion. So we either need to have clearer docs, or some type of run time warning.

Agreed, but albedo_0 shouldn't interfere with albedo_1 since they have different names, should they? If so, then why would they show up as different uniforms in the editor. I get that two shaders, both with a unique uniform with name color_0 should share value, but to one called 'elephant' in one shader and one 'unicorn' in another shader randomly being assigned to either the value of elephant or unicorn makes little sense to me.

Ran into this issue but I now understand that it has to be this way Important bit is: The names are just fluff basically The instance uniform index is what matters. If you don't specify the index manually using the `instance uniform vec4 my_color : source_color, instance_index(5);` thing (from docs), that index is just assigned automatically based on the amount of instance uniforms in this shader (first instance uniform has index 0, second one is 1, etc) Why not make the same names have the same index? Because its impossible to gurantee this. Different meshes might have multiple surfaces with multiple different shaders with different instance uniform setups but with some overlapping names. Godot would somehow have to solve this giant puzzle of making sure every instance uniform with the same name in every shader is using the same index (and the limit is only 16) A solution for your example is very simple: you need to assign indices manually First shader: `instance uniform vec3 color_0: source_color, instance_index(0);` Second shader: `instance uniform vec3 color_1: source_color, instance_index(1);` And now the issue will be solved. How can Godot help with this? I think the docs already make it pretty clear how it works. That's how I figured it My proposed solution(s): - Force the user to always specify an index for the instance uniform. This would make it obvious that the index is important and that it shouldn't overlap. But this is obviously a breaking change - Show the index in UI near the uniform name. It would look like this roughly: This would make it very obvious when there are 2 uniforms that have the same index. But there might be a problem if the same uniform name is used in 2 different shaders with different indices. I dunno if there is a good solution for this (show 2 entries? with same name but different indx) - Show a misconfiguration warning if a MeshInstance3D has instance uniforms that share the same index but have different names (this is probably not what user intended)
